Doing more with less

81

NGOs had closed at least one office by April 2025, after the US aid cuts.

Stroup & Hadden, The Conversation (Jan 2026), citing Devex

And AI is everywhere already

Almost everyone uses it. Few see the difference.

92%

of nonprofits use AI in some way

7%

of those see major improvements in their mission

Virtuous, 2026 Nonprofit AI Adoption Report: industry survey of 346 nonprofits, December 2025

The question isn't whether to use AI.

It's what it's actually good for, and what it still can't do for you.

What AI can do for sustainability work, now

Three things it already does well

It sees

Watching ecosystems at a scale no team could.

It warns

Forecasting floods and weather before they hit.

It talks

Advice, translation and paperwork, in people's own language.

It sees · Wildlife

AI sorts the photos. People check what it found.

Millions of camera-trap photos

animal · species suggested
CAM-07 · 03:41

SpeciesNet's first pass

A person verifies

SpeciesNet is open source and in The Nature Conservancy's Animl platform. Okala adds sound (Google's Perch) to watch and listen across several African countries.

Google Research, March 2026

It sees · Forests

From counting what's lost to predicting what's at risk

Then

Where was forest lost?

Now

What drove the loss?

Next

Where is it at risk?

Global Forest Watch and Google DeepMind now map the drivers of forest loss, locally to globally. New maps also separate natural forest from plantations, which deforestation-free supply-chain rules need.

Google Research: forecasting forest loss; natural-forest maps

It warns · Floods

Flood forecasts where there are no river gauges

2 bn+people covered by river-flood forecasts
150countries
24 hwarning of urban flash floods, new in 2026

The flash-flood model learned from news reports of past floods.

Google Flood Hub · Google Research, 12 March 2026

Photo: Manila street, Judgefloro, public domain, Wikimedia Commons

It warns · Weather

1,000×

less energy per forecast. Europe's weather centre has run an AI forecast model since 25 February 2025.

That's what opens it up to countries without supercomputers.

ECMWF, February 2025 and May 2026 (AIFS v2)

AI model

Producing the forecast the physics way

It talks · Farm advice

An extension officer in every pocket

Digital Green's FarmerChat answers smallholders by text, voice or photo. Answers come from expert-vetted advice, not the open internet.

200,000+farmers in Kenya alone, by March 2026
6languages, 40+ crops, 4 countries
600 villagesin a randomised trial in Nakuru County, Kenya, testing whether it raises yields and incomes. Results after March 2027.

Digital Green & Microsoft Research (2024) · ICT4D 2026 · AEA RCT Registry 0017035

Farm adviceanswers from vetted sources
Spots on my maize leaves. What is it?
It may be a leaf disease. Can you tell me when the spots first appeared?
Thank you. Here is what extension officers recommend…

Illustrative conversation, not a real exchange

It talks · Your desk

Where most of you will see value first

Draft

Proposals, reports, donor updates

Translate

Between your team, partners and funders

Summarise

Long documents into what matters to you

Search research

Elicit, Consensus and similar, built on open data

They do the first pass. They don't do the checking.

Where it falls short

Four honest limits

Usage isn't impact

4%

of nonprofit people say AI is fully integrated where they work

NTEN survey of 900+ people, Sept 2026

Skills are the barrier, and small teams are behind

Large charities
82%
Small charities
52%

Everyday AI use · 56% name skills as the top barrier · Charity Digital Skills Report 2026 (UK)

It has a footprint

+17%

data-centre electricity in 2025, roughly doubling by 2030

IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI, April 2026

It makes things up, confidently

Every tool we've shown keeps a person checking.

GoogleDeepMindECMWFDigital Green

Big models, increasingly free to use. None of them answers:

Who already knows how to solve my problem, and will they talk to me?

The gap AI hasn't closed

Knowing, but not doing

Studies that identified priority areas for conservation:

discussed putting it into practice
29.5%
documented action actually taken
5.7%

The figure is old, and that's the point: the gap has been named for nearly 20 years.

Knight et al. 2008, Conservation Biology, as cited by Groff et al. 2023

When evidence reaches people

45.7%

of interventions: that's how many each of 92 conservation managers changed their likelihood of using, after reading a short evidence summary.

Walsh, Dicks & Sutherland 2015, Conservation Biology · stated intent, not observed decisions

But access alone isn't enough

Practitioners also need

Time

Funding

Skilled people

Sabo et al. 2024, Frontiers in Conservation Science

Donella Meadows' story

Same houses. Different place for the meter.

Meter in the basement

Meter in the front hall

30%

lower electricity use where people could see the meter

Donella Meadows, Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System (1999), told as "the story goes"

Places to intervene in a system

Who can see the information changes how the system behaves.

We want to put an NGO's problem where the expert can see it.

Meadows (1999): 12 leverage points, 1 the most effective. Labels shortened.

12Numbers and parameters
11Buffers
10Stock-and-flow structures
9Delays
8Balancing feedback loops
7Reinforcing feedback loops
6The structure of information flows
5The rules of the system
4The power to self-organise
3The goals of the system
2The paradigm
1Transcending paradigms
